item.text: {"case_id":"SPR00419","decision":"candidate","candidate_ranking":["C09","C14","C05"],"selected_candidate_label":"C09","confidence":0.74,"relationship_type":"structural_functional_template","rationale":"C09 plausibly supplied a material argumentative template for the child: an ongoing dam or flood-control project should not be halted despite opposition or calls for further review, because delay would sacrifice urgently needed flood protection and disrupt orderly construction already underway. The child adapts that machinery to Kinzua Dam and then adds a distinct mitigation program for the displaced Seneca Nation. C14 and C05 share the water-project review setting and some decision structure, but both primarily advocate postponing authorization pending further study, making them weaker templates for the child's decision to proceed.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"the cessation of construction would, of course, delay the providing of essential protection","parent_excerpt":"There is no economy in spending less than we can afford on our efforts to stop these disastrous floods.","explanation":"Both use the urgency of flood protection as a central reason against stopping or delaying dam construction."},{"child_excerpt":"I have concluded that it is not possible to halt the construction of Kinzua Dam currently under way.","parent_excerpt":"The effect of this reduction would be to stop construction on a number of projects now underway, to slow down work on many others","explanation":"Both focus concretely on the harmful consequences of interrupting projects already under construction."},{"child_excerpt":"all of the alternative proposals that have been suggested...have been thoroughly and fairly examined and are clearly inferior to the Kinzua project","parent_excerpt":"it provides no excuse whatever for failing to proceed with projects which we now know are sound and beneficial and urgently needed","explanation":"Both answer demands for alternatives or additional study by asserting that an established, urgently needed project should proceed."},{"child_excerpt":"Impounding of the funds appropriated by the Congress after long and exhaustive Congressional review...would not be proper.","parent_excerpt":"The proper way...is to move forward steadily, year by year, toward the orderly and economic completion of projects now underway","explanation":"The child adapts C09's orderly-continuation rationale to the specific institutional facts of congressional appropriations and completed judicial review."}]}
